n: This short, personal message to Baruch goes back to Jehoiakim’s fourth year (605 BC), when Baruch first wrote Jeremiah’s prophecies on a scroll. It may be placed here as a kind of signature to the story of Jeremiah’s life.

f.w: when he had written these words in a book

n: God has a word specifically for Baruch. The Lord notices the faithful helpers behind the scenes.
Baruch had cried, “Woe is me! The Lord has added grief to my pain; I’m exhausted with groaning and find no rest.” Writing and reading those warnings had cost him dearly.

f.g: I am worn out with groaning.

n: God’s answer: I am tearing down what I built and uprooting what I planted—the whole land. God himself feels the loss too.

f.w: that which I have built will I break down

n: “Are you seeking great things for yourself? Don’t.” Baruch, from a notable family, may have had ambitions for prominence. In a time of collapse, the greatest gift is life itself—and God promises he will keep Baruch alive wherever he goes.

f.w: seekest thou great things for thyself?
thy life will I give unto thee for a prey
